claims.text: Depositing the alloy on a substrate with a mismatched lattice parameter introduces controllable lattice strain.
Lattice strain alters magnetostructural transition dynamics in as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys.
Strain-altered magnetostructural transition dynamics reduce hysteresis.
Strain-altered magnetostructural transition dynamics improve the magnetocaloric response.
The predicted reductions in hysteresis and improvements in magnetocaloric response occur during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
The relevant comparison baseline is the same as-deposited alloy without intentionally introduced lattice strain.
The proposed strain intervention can be implemented without adding rare-earth elements.
The predicted effects hold while mechanical stability is retained.
Changing substrate lattice parameters should produce corresponding changes in magnetocaloric response and hysteresis.
An absence of significant changes in both magnetocaloric response and hysteresis as lattice strain is varied would falsify the hypothesis.
The magnitude of the strain effect on magnetocaloric response and hysteresis is uncertain.
